## Purpose and Public Entry Points
cuVSLAM is a C++/CUDA SDK for real-time visual odometry, visual-inertial odometry, and SLAM across mono, RGB-D, stereo/multicamera, inertial, and multisensor rigs. The primary public API is the cuVSLAM library and tracker surface in `libs/cuvslam/cuvslam2.h`, implemented by `libs/cuvslam/cuvslam2.cpp` and `libs/cuvslam/tracker.cpp`. Python bindings expose that API through `python/cuvslam2.cpp`; runnable C++ and Python integrations are under `examples/` and `tools/`.

## Sensor, Dataset, and Calibration Boundary
Callers provide calibrated camera rigs, timestamped images, and optionally IMU/depth data. Core camera geometry, observations, coordinate systems, and IMU primitives reside in `libs/camera/rig.h`, `libs/camera/observation.h`, and `libs/common/imu_measurement.h`. EDEX is the repository’s offline sensor-sequence interchange format, read/written by `libs/edex/edex.h` and used by dataset examples and evaluation tools. ROS bags can be converted at the tooling boundary via `tools/python_tools/cuvslam_tools/bag2edex/`.

## Front-End Tracking and GPU Compute
The visual front end constructs image/gradient pyramids, detects/selects features, and tracks them across frames; it supports CPU and CUDA implementations behind SOF interfaces. Key modules are `libs/sof/sof.h`, `libs/sof/sof_create.cpp`, and `libs/sof/sof_multicamera_gpu.cpp`. CUDA kernels and wrappers provide high-throughput image processing, KLT/stereo tracking, feature selection, ICP, and GPU bundle adjustment in `libs/cuda_modules/cuda_kernels/`, `libs/cuda_modules/lk_tracker.cpp`, and `libs/cuda_modules/sba.cpp`.

## Estimation Pipelines and Odometry Modes
Pipeline classes convert tracked features and sensor inputs into incremental poses, manage tracker state, triangulation, PnP, and optimization services. This orchestration is centered in `libs/pipelines/tracker_state_machine.cpp`, `libs/pipelines/track_online_multi.cpp`, and `libs/pipelines/track_online_multisensor.cpp`. Mode-specific odometry adapters implement mono, RGB-D, multicamera, stereo-inertial, and multisensor behavior in `libs/odometry/mono_visual_odometry.cpp`, `libs/odometry/rgbd_odometry.cpp`, and `libs/odometry/multisensor_odometry.cpp`. Geometric estimation is separated into epipolar/PnP/math layers, including `libs/epipolar/fundamental_matrix_utils.cpp` and `libs/pnp/multisensor_pose_estimator.cpp`.

## Inertial Fusion and Refinement
IMU calibration/preintegration and inertial optimization feed visual-inertial modes, with implementations in `libs/imu/imu_preintegration.cpp`, `libs/imu/inertial_optimization.cpp`, and `libs/pipelines/imu_fusion_context.cpp`. Local nonlinear refinement and bundle adjustment have CPU/GPU paths in `libs/refinement/refinement.cpp`, `libs/sba/schur_complement_bundler_gpu.cpp`, and the CUDA SBA kernels. Multisensor mode depends on the cuNLS-enabled build path.

## SLAM, Map Persistence, and Localization
Tracking can feed asynchronous SLAM workers that build keyframes/landmarks, detect loop closures, optimize pose graphs, and localize against saved maps. The control boundary is `libs/slam/async_slam/async_slam.cpp`; core SLAM state and map building are in `libs/slam/slam/slam.cpp` and `libs/slam/slam/slam_map_building.cpp`. Persistent SLAM map storage is abstracted through `libs/slam/map/database/slam_database.h` with LMDB implementation in `libs/slam/map/database/lmdb_slam_database.cpp`. A simpler mapping service also exists in `libs/map/map.h` and `libs/map/service.h`.

## Build, Runtime, and Integrations
CMake builds the native libraries from `CMakeLists.txt` and `libs/CMakeLists.txt`; Python packaging links against the built shared library via `python/setup.py`. Material runtime dependencies are CUDA 12/13, C++/Python runtimes, and optional LMDB, Rerun visualization, NVTX, and cuNLS. External sources are pinned under `cmake/ext/`, notably `cmake/ext/cunls.cmake` and `cmake/ext/lmdb.cmake`. Operational entry points include `tools/cuvslam_api_launcher/cuvslam_api_launcher.cpp`, `tools/tracker/tracker.cpp`, and hardware/dataset examples such as `examples/realsense/run_vio.py`.
